review.statement: The phase, capabilities, workstreams, limits, repository-backed application deployment claim, completed M-18 retirement record, documentation automation, and isolated-worktree guidance were reviewed together against origin/main commit 0f8f65f, the completed A04 contract commit 1ca7d5c, the accepted A05 correction commit 6eb303e, and the corrected A06 contract sources and evidence in this review. The Core operator-panel and exploratory hosted-service roadmap now include completed A01 feature ownership, A02 threat modeling, accepted A03 boundary decisions, A04's versioned workspace and actor vocabulary, A05's adapter-neutral configuration lifecycle and recovery contracts, and A06's closed stream/mode/format catalog, bounded upload/shared/connected admission, exact workspace binding, normalized provenance, explicit freshness, finite consent/grant state, and executable commit-only-verified last-known-good behavior. The A06 network policy is a dependency-free conservative CIDR table reviewed on 2026-08-31 against the current official IANA IPv4/IPv6 special-purpose, IPv4 address-space, and IPv6 Global Unicast allocation registries. IPv6 targets are positive-listed only from current ALLOCATED prefixes and then filtered through the special-purpose deny table; unlisted theoretical 2000::/3 space remains denied. The registry update dates and re-review condition are recorded. Source attempts require strictly increasing chronology, equal timestamps reject deterministically with detached prior state, active grants are bounded by issuance and expiry, consent transactions have an exported 10-minute maximum lifetime, and committed projection admission validates coherent acquisition/commit/freshness/attempt relationships. Focused compile-time and runtime evidence covers allocated/reserved IPv6 boundaries, content/path/media denial, SSRF/rebinding, exact/overlong consent lifetimes, premature/partial/expired grants, same-ID tenant substitution, older/equal attempts, contradictory committed state, unavailable/degraded/stale transitions, JSON safety, and post-construction mutation. The panel runtime, source parsers/fetchers, OAuth clients, persistence adapters, current SQLite schema, and package restructuring remain unchanged; A07-A08 are still required for the architecture-ready gate. Landing-page and synthetic-display worktrees remain separately owned, and no new live application, provider, route, or service probe was performed.

project.milestone: M-18 completed; legacy app and migration shadow retired to cold recovery
project.summary: The standalone Chalkwright service is documented as the classroom display source of truth. The legacy app and migration shadow are retired from active service with cold-recovery artifacts retained. Current repository work continues on post-retirement stabilization, roadmap design, demonstration reproducibility, synthetic fixture presentation, and the self-documenting development workflow.

deployment.summary: Repository evidence says the standalone production lane serves the existing classroom display path, provider acquisition and owned-Calendar follower jobs are active, and M-18 retired the legacy app and migration shadow from active service while retaining cold-recovery artifacts.
deployment.evidenceBasis: Reviewed repository documentation through origin/main commit 0f8f65f, including the completed M-18 record. This semantic refresh performed no new application-service, provider, credential, route, or classroom-display probe.

priorities: Observe post-retirement production stability and preserve the retained cold-recovery evidence and explicit restoration boundary.
Make the repository's present state, capabilities, workstreams, limitations, and verification status continuously available to Codex.
Advance the Core operator panel through its remaining A07-A08 architecture gate before package restructuring or UI implementation.
Keep privacy-safe demonstration work reproducible, accessible, independently versioned, and operationally separate from application releases.
Continue bounded enrichment work for learning objectives, lesson references, vocabulary, and setup usability without broadening provider authority.
knownLimits: General installation support and public-production readiness for external adopters are not claimed.
M-18 removed the active legacy and shadow fallbacks; any temporary cold-recovery restoration now requires explicit incident authorization and must be disabled again after the bounded recovery window.
PowerSchool and Google Classroom remain read-only; Calendar writes remain limited to verified application-owned events.

Semantic documentation accuracy is a mandatory model-reviewed completion condition; documented deployment claims still require a separately authorized live probe before being reported as current live state.

The current strict runtime configuration is not yet the intended guided end-user setup experience. A04-A06 define workspace/actor, configuration-state, and source-mode contract surfaces, but no source parser, fetcher, OAuth client, persistence adapter, route, UI, or use case implements those new contracts yet and current SQLite schemas and runtime behavior are unchanged.

The A06 shared-resource CIDR policy is a reviewed conservative snapshot, not a dynamic future-registry claim. The theoretical 2000::/3 IPv6 envelope is not treated as allocated: only current IANA IPv6 Global Unicast ALLOCATED rows are positive-listed before special-purpose subtraction. Re-review is required before shared-resource implementation and whenever a referenced IANA registry updates.
nextDecisions: What post-retirement observation interval and evidence should close the remaining stabilization period without weakening the cold-recovery boundary.
What maintenance and contribution workflow should govern the separate landing page as Chalkwright approaches broader installation support.

Which operator-panel navigation, page contracts, guidance, readiness, planned-display review, responsive/accessibility requirements, and hosted presentation seams A07 should establish without assuming Core account authentication.

capabilities.name: Canonical schedule and day-plan orchestration
capabilities.summary: Normalizes trusted schedule observations into a provider-neutral canonical day plan and derives deterministic effective plans.
capabilities.safety: Provider observations are read-only inputs; invalid or unavailable observations fail closed and preserve last-known-good state.

capabilities.name: Schedule-aware classroom display
capabilities.summary: Serves responsive morning, coming-up, check-in, in-class, transition, dismissal, gap, and day-complete views with deterministic timing.
capabilities.safety: The fixture route is loopback-only by default; production serving and route changes remain separately controlled.

capabilities.name: PowerSchool schedule acquisition
capabilities.summary: Acquires bounded bell and schedule data through passive, manual-repair, just-in-time-repair, and compatibility lanes.
capabilities.safety: PowerSchool is strictly read-only; browser/session repair is isolated from normal collection and protected state remains outside Git.

capabilities.name: Google Classroom assignment enrichment
capabilities.summary: Refreshes read-only Classroom coursework into a local cache and projects relevant assignments without blocking display responses.
capabilities.safety: Scopes and adapters are read-only; provider failure retains cached content and cannot create or modify coursework.

capabilities.name: Application-owned Calendar reconciliation
capabilities.summary: Projects the canonical plan into explicitly owned Calendar events with a single writer, leases, journals, receipts, idempotency, and rollback evidence.
capabilities.safety: Writes are limited to exact configured targets and verified Chalkwright-owned events; unrelated events and calendars are denied.

capabilities.name: Meeting-scoped attendance check-in presentation
capabilities.summary: Presents class-scoped attendance links, response context, and QR codes for students to use on their own devices.
capabilities.safety: Chalkwright displays check-in context but does not submit attendance to PowerSchool or another school system.

capabilities.name: Learning objectives, lesson references, and vocabulary
capabilities.summary: Imports bounded teacher-authored objectives and glossary data, selects deterministic vocabulary, and displays multilingual lesson content.
capabilities.safety: Imports are bounded and provenance-aware; ambiguity preserves prior fallbacks and no LLM or provider write is required.

capabilities.name: Preview, overrides, and carousel controls
capabilities.summary: Supports future or frozen-time preview, scoped local overrides, and server-controlled carousel holds isolated by screen and date.
capabilities.safety: Preview and report-only paths cannot acquire mutation authority; override scope is validated and persisted locally.

capabilities.name: Durable state, recovery, and last-known-good behavior
capabilities.summary: Uses SQLite migrations, integrity checks, backups, retention, restart-safe jobs, and last-known-good projections. A05 additionally defines the future adapter-neutral revision lifecycle, exact optimistic concurrency, redacted export, protected-backup admission, forward migration, and rollback contracts without changing current storage; returned plans and applied snapshots detach canonical JSON data from caller-owned inputs.
capabilities.safety: Credentials and browser profiles stay outside SQLite and Git; recovery paths validate state before activation. Future configuration adapters must preserve the active revision on conflict or failure, compare full workspace kind/ID/installation-or-organization identity, reject same-ID tenant substitution, and expose only opaque protected-secret references.

capabilities.name: Immutable production deployment and rollback
capabilities.summary: Builds digest-bound releases, polls protected main, verifies readiness, switches atomically, and rolls back failed releases.
capabilities.safety: Merge, deployment, route, and activation effects remain explicitly authorized operations with fail-closed gates.

capabilities.name: School branding and bounded site media
capabilities.summary: Supports an installation-specific school logo, course art, countdown media, local validation, and digest-pinned serving.
capabilities.safety: Remote inputs become owner-only validated local files; public repository media remains synthetic or provenance-gated.

capabilities.name: Synthetic local evaluation and public demonstration
capabilities.summary: Provides a loopback-only B407 demonstration, reproducible screenshots, privacy-safe fixture evidence, smoke checks, and disposable rehearsals.
capabilities.safety: Fixtures and captures contain no student, provider, credential, private-route, or production database data.

capabilities.name: Guided non-secret installation configuration
capabilities.summary: Provide a private-by-default Core operator panel for versioned configuration, guided sources, readiness, and planned-display review while retaining strict generated runtime contracts. A04 established the shared workspace and actor vocabulary; A05 established immutable detached configuration lifecycle and recovery contracts; and A06 now establishes every source stream's exact four-mode disposition, closed first-release formats and budgets, bounded upload/shared/connected admission, finite read-only consent/grant states, normalized provenance, explicit freshness, and commit-only-verified last-known-good behavior. The panel, adapters, OAuth clients, and persistence remain planned.
capabilities.safety: Core adds no account login, so operator reachability confers full authority. Accepted ADR-0026 requires a separate operator process on an explicit loopback address or Unix socket by default, isolated from display routes, identity, cookies, cache, readiness, and storage capabilities. Provider grants, OAuth material, tokens, browser profiles, and private values remain separate from portable non-secret configuration.

capabilities.name: Historical shadow retirement
capabilities.summary: M-18 retired the original Classroom Screen runtime and migration shadow from active service while preserving source, state, unit definitions, route snapshots, and rollback instructions as cold-recovery evidence.
capabilities.safety: Cold recovery requires explicit incident authorization, may restore only the named retained route and service, and must disable the legacy path again after the bounded recovery window.

capabilities.name: Attendance administration workflow
capabilities.summary: An operator-facing attendance administration workflow remains deliberately outside the current production scope.
capabilities.safety: Any future workflow must preserve read-only school-system boundaries and must not infer authority from existing aggregate continuity data.

workstreams.name: Obsessively self-documenting development workflow
workstreams.outcome: Keep semantic project state and capability knowledge current, enforced, and directly available inside every Codex task.
workstreams.currentState: The generated documentation router, tiered session and prompt hooks, quiet resume/compaction host refresh, path watcher, timer, semantic state registry, implementation-fingerprint gate, workstream classification, and isolated-worktree guidance are implemented in this branch and installed on the canonical host.
nextSteps: Maintain the registry and relevant durable prose with every implementation change, acknowledge each new implementation fingerprint only after semantic review, and keep the complete verification chain green.

workstreams.name: Privacy-safe homepage demonstration
workstreams.outcome: Produce reproducible, accessible, privacy-safe media that explains Chalkwright accurately on the separate public landing page.
workstreams.currentState: Synthetic storyboards, narration/render tooling, provenance boundaries, and landing-page operating instructions remain an active application-repository workstream. The published 123-second native-1080p cut follows one coherent day: Web Design appears in the first coming-up state and completes its class sequence before the later Robotics sequence and Robotics dismissal. Its Web Design opening uses a measured natural clause pause; the Classroom-to-vocabulary handoff uses a short continuous breath without a fade. Every captured display state uses the ChalkWright logo as the unconfigured school-brand placeholder. The Robotics sequence animates its explicitly labeled Google Classroom assignment, task details, and due date before its translation faces; the assignment remains stable through the edit instead of beginning an automatic card advance during its final frames. The translation faces remain synchronized to narration-topic boundaries without repeating the language enumeration. Displayed demo branding uses ChalkWright casing, the schedule narration says the day's complete schedule, and the closing voice explicitly says Apache two point oh. This corrected cut is live at chalkwright.org with accurate default-on captions and a dedicated visible CC toggle. A newer unpublished 123-second candidate removes the unspoken fourth overview bullet, retimes each anatomy callout to lead its matching spoken phrase by about 0.2 seconds, lets the final full-screen pullback settle after narration, introduces the second class with the authentic Robotics coming-up display before dissolving during the spoken pause into its objective, and shortens the following narration to avoid repeating the Robotics class name. The landing page's separate private repository uses main as the default branch and records the deployed source at commit 7a4a9f207ff46c21092f8f7aef855c018e8095d8. The Lenovo origin and public Cloudflare route were verified on 2026-08-30, including exact video and caption hashes, text/vtt caption delivery, HTTP 206 video ranges and a zero-finding production dependency audit. Authorized capacity recovery and publication cleanup removed superseded build cache and predecessor images; the current live image and canonical source remain intact, with no predecessor image retained. Future landing-page changes require their canonical application documentation and semantic-state handoff within the same task.
nextSteps: Maintain reproducible media provenance, caption accuracy, public delivery checks and independent landing-page source history as the demonstration evolves.

workstreams.name: Synthetic display-content polish
workstreams.outcome: Keep fixture-backed captures representative of current objectives, assignments, and multilingual vocabulary without introducing private classroom data.
workstreams.currentState: The B407 synthetic fixture and preview evidence include richer Web Design and Robotics carousel content. Coursework retains an explicit Google Classroom presentation, the Robotics assignment includes synthetic task and due-date details, and an unconfigured school-brand slot uses the ChalkWright placeholder logo; corresponding display assertions are updated.
nextSteps: Verify the accepted viewport envelope and regenerate only reproducible synthetic preview evidence when presentation behavior changes.

workstreams.name: Core configuration panel and hosted-shell planning
workstreams.outcome: Move the agreed Core operator panel and related hosted-shell direction through an architecture-ready, measurable implementation gate without changing live runtime behavior prematurely.
workstreams.currentState: A01 through A06 are complete. The authoritative feature acceptance matrix freezes product ownership; the threat model defines 32 stable threats, security invariants, residual-risk dispositions, and 18 negative-test families; accepted ADR-0026 fixes the package, artifact, process, compatibility, and presentation seam; A04 defines the versioned workspace and actor vocabulary; A05 defines immutable detached configuration lifecycle and recovery contracts; and corrected A06 defines the complete source stream/mode/release matrix, closed stream-specific formats, concrete item/transaction budgets, actual-content upload/media admission, bounded per-hop shared-resource SSRF evidence, consent transactions capped at 10 minutes, finite read-only provider grants, normalized observation/projection provenance, explicit mode-specific freshness, and executable commit-only-verified last-known-good transitions. The network policy is a dependency-free conservative CIDR table reviewed against the current official IANA IPv4/IPv6 special-purpose, IPv4 address-space, and IPv6 Global Unicast allocation registries with a recorded re-review condition. IPv6 admission positive-lists only current ALLOCATED prefixes and subtracts special-purpose ranges, so unlisted theoretical 2000::/3 space remains denied. Strict source-attempt chronology rejects older and equal timestamps with detached prior state, connected reads require active grants at/after issuance and before expiry, and committed state validates coherent acquisition/commit/freshness/attempt relationships. Focused compile-time and runtime tests cover self-hosted and hosted fixtures, exact-workspace collisions, path/active/archive/content denial, normalized media, allocated/reserved/documentation/returned/mixed/rebinding/peer network boundaries, exact/overlong consent lifetimes, premature/partial/expired grants, older/equal attempts, contradictory committed state, unavailable/degraded/stale outcomes, malformed values, JSON safety, and post-construction mutation aliases. These contracts are not yet threaded into use cases or adapters; no parser, fetcher, OAuth client, route, UI, current SQLite schema, or runtime behavior changed. The M-18-aware roadmap and 49-task dependency-ordered work breakdown remain governing. No package restructuring, operator/display process, artifact, operator route, provider enrollment, hosted repository, billing integration, or deployment has begun.
nextSteps: Execute A07 to specify Core operator-panel navigation, pages, guidance, readiness, planned-display review, responsive/accessibility behavior, and hosted presentation seams without assuming Core login UI.
Complete A08 after A07, and do not begin Phase B until the architecture-ready gate is satisfied.
